promise: Turn observed recurring agent mistakes into small cues only when evidence supports their use.
audience: People evaluating and improving recurring agent behavior.
trigger: Investigate a repeated correction or evaluate a proposed behavioral cue.

modes.name: Observe
modes.output: Consented structural observations and a falsifiable cue hypothesis.

modes.name: Assess
modes.when: A candidate cue has probe cases.
modes.output: A paired evidence record including no-effect and uncertainty.

modes.name: Maintain
modes.when: A cue is active, stale or harmful.
modes.output: An evidence-gated lifecycle decision and traceable ledger state.

examples.title: Assess a source-reference cue
examples.brief: Use Preceptor to assess a proposed cue for a fictional agent that repeatedly omits a requested source reference. Define the opportunity and violation, a cue/no-cue probe and a task-quality check. Keep it a candidate until the native evidence gate is satisfied.
examples.before: A one-off correction becomes a permanent prompt rule with no control group.
examples.after: A small cue remains proposed until paired probes support a useful effect.
examples.why: No-effect and inconclusive records can prevent unsupported prompt growth.

boundaries: A minimum sample count and passing gate are not independent proof of efficacy or generalization.

marketing.headline: Keep agent guidance that earns its place.
marketing.lead: For people maintaining an agent’s recurring instructions. Preceptor turns repeated corrections into small testable cues, compares cue and no-cue behavior, and keeps inconclusive evidence from becoming permanent guidance.

benefits.title: Focus on a recurring mistake
benefits.body: Start with observed opportunities and violations instead of turning one failure into a universal rule.

benefits.title: Test the cue’s contribution
benefits.body: Compare behavior with and without the cue, retaining no-effect and harmful outcomes.

benefits.title: Keep the lifecycle inspectable
benefits.body: Use the native ledger and read-only gate preview to see why a cue remains a candidate, is promoted or can be retired.

walkthrough.title: Observe with consent
walkthrough.detail: Collect the structural evidence needed for a specific behavior; optional telemetry never records message or file text.

walkthrough.title: Compare the alternatives
walkthrough.detail: Name a small cue and run matched probes with and without it, measuring task quality as well as compliance.

walkthrough.title: Maintain through the ledger
walkthrough.detail: Use the tool API for lifecycle writes. Preserve human-origin and pinned cue protections and leave inconclusive candidates undecided.

use_when: The same correction recurs and you want to test a targeted instruction.
An agent’s guidance has grown and individual cues need an evidence review.
You need a trace of why a behavioral cue changed status.
not_for: Automatically recording people because the skill is installed.
Claiming a cue helps because the agent repeated its wording.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Preceptor to assess a proposed cue for a fictional agent that repeatedly omits a requested source reference. Define the opportunity and violation, a cue/no-cue probe and a task-quality check. Keep it a candidate until the native evidence gate is satisfied.
marketing.output_preview:
Candidate cue: include the source reference when the task requires one
Behavior: reference omission on an eligible answer
Probe arms: cue / no cue
Quality check: answer remains correct and supported

Gate preview: inconclusive until sufficient comparative evidence exists
Action: retain candidate status; do not promote from one correction
marketing.example_note: Fictional cue proposal. There are no measured runs or promotion results in this example.
install_notes: Python 3.11 or later is required by the portable install/build helper. The installed method runs through your agent host.
The portable method is independent of an observation service.
For native ledger inspection install modules/tool-preceptor and use project-preceptor --help.
Live observation or cue injection requires the optional host composition and its consent controls.
marketing.proof_summary: Native ledger and lifecycle tests check gate behavior and protections. Minimum run counts alone do not establish statistical power or behavioral benefit.
marketing.next_step: Choose one recurring correction and define a comparison before adding another permanent instruction.

film.heading: One more rock.
film.blurb: In 70 seconds, Bramble the pack mule carries every rule anyone ever added, until nobody knows which ones still do anything. Preceptor starts from the mistake that actually happened, writes one small cue, keeps it out of the pack and races two Brambles on the same tasks. Too close to call means the cue stays a candidate. Taking a rule out needs proof too. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The agent, the tasks and the race result are a fictional example. Five runs each is a minimum, not proof; the film shows how the skill behaves and reports no results.
